requirements.requirement: Repair bin/replay so pending messages are delivered exactly once per Message-ID while retaining distinct messages that share a subject.
requirements.summary: The repaired executable delivered one copy each of <a@branch.test> and <b@branch.test>, retained the pre-existing <old@branch.test>, and preserved both distinct Notice-subject messages. The final index contained exactly those three unique IDs.

requirements.requirement: On subsequent recovery runs, skip messages already recorded in delivered/index.tsv.
requirements.summary: A rerun produced no delivered/quarantine hash differences and left the index at three unique IDs. The same idempotence check passed again after restart.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the original spool and the already-delivered message.
requirements.summary: All four seeded spool files remained with their baseline hashes; delivered old.eml remained present and indexed. Post-restart checks again found four spool messages and healthy recovery data.

requirements.requirement: Place malformed messages in quarantine with an explanation.
requirements.summary: The source inspection established that bad.eml lacked a Message-ID. It was copied intact to quarantine with a reason explaining that replay was refused due to a missing, duplicate, or malformed Message-ID header.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were observed before and after the work and restart. The POSIX-shell replay passed /bin/sh syntax checks and executed successfully on that platform.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was also complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were captured, restart was acknowledged, unavailability was observed, the boot identity changed, and SSH plus replay/data state recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the transition. Minor hygiene residue consists only of five retained /tmp evidence files.
limitations: No final byte-for-byte comparison of old.eml against its seeded hash was captured; preservation is supported by its continued presence, Message-ID/subject, unchanged index association, and replay behavior.

The lifecycle package-health probe invoked an unsupported yum operation, and systemd failed-service inspection was unavailable on this legacy host, limiting broad package/service hygiene assessment; neither conflicts with the task-specific evidence.
Requirement R3 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: The substantive mutations—replacing replay, correcting its index parsing, executing recovery, and restarting for the mandatory protocol—had clear roles in implementation or verification. The only unnecessary retained mutations were five low-risk temporary artifacts: /tmp/replay-state-before and /tmp/replay-state-after from cmd-6f60da3c31cb403f, /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log from cmd-2ef3d41b60d74341, and /tmp/postboot-before and /tmp/postboot-after from cmd-2146f46b6ad04519. None was cleaned up; no reverted unnecessary mutations were identified. Failed SSH probes during the bounded restart were read-only and are not hygiene faults.
